div.head: Rect 4.6
div.ab: [4.6] Hede se ðe scire healde, þæt he wite á, hwæt ealdlandræden sy ⁊ hwæt ðeode ðeaw.
Uideat qui scyram tenet, ut semper sciat, que sit antiqua terrarum institutio uel populi consuetudo.
On suman ealugafol . hede se ðe scire healde þæt he wite a hwæt ealdland ræden sy . 7hwæt ealdland ræden sy 7 hwæt ðeode ðeaw.
Hede se ðe scire healde þæt he wite a hwæt ealdland ræden sy and hwæt ðeode ðeaw.
Achte wer das [Gutsvogtei]amt inne hat, dass er stets wisse, was [echte] alte Gutsordnung und was Landesgewohnheit ist!
Let him who holds the [reeve's] office take heed that he always knows what the [true] ancient estate-custom is and what the custom of the people!
In some estates ale-rent. He that would hold a shire should heed that he know what the old estate customs and what the customs of the region are.
The person who would oversee a shire should always take care to know what the previous estate agreements were and what the local customs are.
div.note: B repeats ‘eald landræden sy ⁊ hwæt’ (a mistaken repetition of the line). eald landræden sy ⁊ hwæt inserted by B: an erroneous repetition of a line

Nicht ‘Landschaft’ (Leo) oder ‘Territorium’ (Andrews 55), missverstanden durch Q (der auch anderes scir als comitatus missversteht III Eg 3. 5, 2), wohl daher Toller 836a III. Richtig ‘Amt’ Schmid; vgl. scirman Ger 5. 12.—Eald hier ‘ehrwürdig, richtig’

Not ‘region’ (Leo) or ‘territory’ (Andrews 55); misunderstood by Q (who also misunderstands other instances of scir as comitatus, III Eg 3. 5, 2), whence probably Toller 836a III. Correctly ‘office’ Schmid; cf. scirman Ger 5. 12.—Eald here means ‘venerable, proper’
‘Volk’ Q Schmid, ‘Gemeinde’ Leo. Laut 21, 1; 2; 4, wo die lokale Bed. besonders klar, heisst þeod hier ‘Landschaft, Gegend’
‘people’ Q Schmid, ‘community’ Leo. According to 21, 1; 2; 4, where the local meaning is especially clear, þeod here means ‘region, district’
